input.question: Why does someone open their mouths when they are feeding someone?
input.ground_truth: People often mimic what they see, especially infants and young children who are still learning how the world works. So the parent feeding them open their mouths with the goal to get the child to mimic it so they can be fed. Eventually the kid gets old enough that you don't have to do this anymore, but by then it has often become a subconscious habit of the parent.

But when someone is *really* feeding another person, like giving them food, they sometimes open their mouth to show how to chew or swallow, or maybe to help guide the food into the other person's mouth. Or sometimes, they open their mouth because they are showing how to do it, just like you show your friend how to do something with a toy.

But most of the time, when feeding someone else, the person *receiving* the food opens their mouth, and the person feeding just watches or helps, but doesn't usually open their own mouth unless they are showing how to do it.

So, someone might open their mouth when feeding someone to show them how to do it, or to help them understand what to do.
